bullets.title: DELL: Massive Q1 beat, FY27 guide raised 38% on AI server surge to $60B
bullets.body: Dell crushed Q1 with revenue of $43.8B (+88% YoY, +23% vs Street $35.7B) and EPS of $4.86 (vs. $2.96 est., +64% beat). AI-optimized server revenue hit $16.1B (+757% YoY) and Q2 guidance came in at $44–45B (vs. $35.1B est.); full-year FY27 revenue guidance raised to $165–169B from $138–142B and EPS to $17.90 from $12.90 (+38%). AI server revenue target lifted to $60B (+144% YoY). Supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, CPUs) are the gating factor, not demand, with backlog extending into FY28. After-hours the stock surged 14–30% across sessions.

bullets.title: MDB: Beat-and-raise, Q2 guide 5% above consensus; AI/Atlas acceleration confirmed
bullets.body: MongoDB reported Q1 revenue of $687.6M (vs. $664.5M consensus) with Atlas +29% YoY; EPS $1.32 vs. $1.19 est. Q2 guidance midpoint of $732M beat by ~$30M (4.5pts), implying Atlas growth acceleration even on tougher compares. FY27 revenue guidance raised to $2.92–2.96B and EPS to $5.95–6.14. Citi maintains Buy with $450 PT (vs. ~$326). After-hours stock was +4–13% depending on the session.

bullets.title: SNOW: +36% on $6B AWS deal and Cortex Code AI acceleration
bullets.body: Snowflake surged ~36% as the $6B commitment to AWS Graviton CPUs and accelerating Cortex Code AI consumption drove a strong Q1 beat and raised FY27 outlook. Product revenue growth is tracking mid-30s with CRPO also accelerating. Dan Ives (Wedbush) called the AWS tie-up a 'game-changer' and views the infrastructure as a competitive moat; stock recovering from $120 lows toward prior $276 highs.

bullets.title: MRVL: Big guidance raise on AI data center; Hedgeye upgrades to #1 long
bullets.body: Marvell delivered an in-line F1Q27 print with a large guidance raise driven by AI interconnect strength; FY27 and FY28 outlooks raised, with FY28 data center guidance viewed as conservative by the Street. Hedgeye upgraded MRVL to its #1 long despite the stock having doubled since the last print. Wolfe hosted a post-earnings pop-up webcast.

bullets.title: ADSK: Q1 beat, FY27 guide raised, acquires MaintainX for $3.6B — stock down 5.5% AH
bullets.body: Autodesk beat Q1 (revenue $1.934B vs. $1.894B est., EPS $2.99 vs. $2.85) and raised FY27 revenue guidance to $8.155–8.215B. The company announced the all-cash acquisition of MaintainX (maintenance/operations SaaS) for $3.6B, which carries $135M+ ARR growing 50%+. The acquisition was the key overhang sending the stock down ~5.5% after-hours.

bullets.title: S (SentinelOne): Modest ARR beat, FY guide in-line, 10% RIF announced — disappoints
bullets.body: SentinelOne's F1Q ARR of $1,163M beat by $3.2M but was below prior quarter's beat quality; Q2 revenue guide of $290M missed the $292M consensus and billings missed by ~$17M. Company announced a 10% workforce reduction (~$25M charge). KeyBanc calls the results 'disappointing' given elevated investor optimism; stock has run +35.8% since Mar 12.

bullets.title: ASAN: F1Q beat and raise; acquires StackAI for $75M; NRR flat at 96%
bullets.body: Asana beat F1Q by $1.5M revenue / $7.5M EBIT and raised FY27 guidance to $859.5M midpoint. The company acquired StackAI (no-code AI agent platform) for $75M, adding ~50bps revenue drag and ~1pt OM drag. A key concern: NRR flat at 96% with zero net new $100k+ customer adds vs. +32 last quarter. Stock +3.9–10% AH. Citi maintains Buy at $13 PT (vs. ~$6.66).

bullets.title: CRM: Conference takeaways bullish on Agent Force H2 ramp; Q1 mixed
bullets.body: At Jefferies conference, Salesforce management flagged H2 2026 acceleration as Agent Force moves from pilot to production, with Agent Force One + Slack expanding TAM. Sales Cloud growth accelerated in Q2. Jim Cramer bullish on CRM at $174, and the stock rallied 8 points intraday. UBS Sector Summary noted F1Q beat but F2Q guidance and cRPO/bookings were disappointing.

bullets.title: HUBS: Non-GAAP margin target hit a year early; AI agents driving demand, short-term sales cycle elongation
bullets.body: HubSpot at Jefferies conference flagged that its 20–22% non-GAAP operating margin target was achieved a year early. Spring Spotlight launched first-party AI agents (support, sales, marketing) with strong initial uptake. SEO-driven content leads declined 27% across customers, driving diversification. Short-term sales cycle elongation expected from agent adoption focus, but outcome-based pricing model is structurally compelling.

bullets.title: WIX: 20% RIF (~1K employees) saves ~$200M/yr; Citi maintains Neutral
bullets.body: Wix confirmed a ~20% workforce reduction impacting 1,000+ employees, targeting ~$200M in annualized cost savings to offset a 16–20% YoY ISL/USD appreciation headwind. Bookings/employee up 14.5% YoY in Q1 via AI leverage. Near-term margin pressure from Base44 AI compute costs and elevated CAC. Citi maintains Neutral/High Risk at $66 PT.

bullets.title: DDOG: Acceleration across all segments; AI observability expansion cited at Bernstein
bullets.body: Datadog at Bernstein flagged growth acceleration across all customer cohorts (not just AI-native), with 13.6% observability market share and room to expand. New products (Bits AI, Totole time-series, security overlays) contribute incrementally. Federal and regulated segments viewed as large untapped opportunity via new deployment models.

bullets.title: SHOP: Adyen added as Shopify Payments processor in UK/France; UBS sees modest near-term impact, strong strategic signal
bullets.body: UBS reports Adyen has been onboarded as a payment processing partner within Shopify Payments for UK and France — Shopify Payments represents 60%+ of Shopify's GMV. Near-term revenue impact is modest (<50bps uplift assuming 25% penetration), but the win signals Adyen's competitive strength in EU. A separate UBS deep-dive estimates Shopify's POS business (~12% of GMV, +30% YoY) could reach ~20% by 2035, contributing 300–500bps to 10-year GMV CAGR.

bullets.title: NVDA: GTC Taipei keynote June 1; co-innovation lab with Lilly; InP laser capacity scaling demand
bullets.body: Jensen Huang teases a 'surprising new product' and will keynote GTC Taipei June 1 on physical AI and scaling infrastructure. NVIDIA and Lilly announced a joint AI lab investing up to $1B over 5 years for drug discovery. Separately, Rosenblatt checks indicate NVIDIA is pushing InP laser capacity to 20x by 2030 (supply chain committed to 12x), and NVIDIA placed additional HBM4 orders with SK Hynix.

bullets.title: SMCI: +14% on Taiwan collaboration story; DELL catch-up trade framing
bullets.body: Super Micro surged ~14% intraday after announcing collaboration with Taiwanese authorities that resulted in 3 arrests related to server technology diversion prevention. Market framed it as a DELL catch-up trade. Skepticism expressed about the need for the announcement, but price action was bullish.

bullets.title: FSLR: Upgraded to Buy at GLJ, PT $315 from $208; technical targets $307 and $317
bullets.body: First Solar was upgraded to Buy at GLJ Research with a price target raised to $315 from $208; stock surged 10.9–11.6%, its strongest single-day advance since May 2025, hitting a new 52-week high. Near-term technical resistance at $306.77 (June 2024 high) and $317 (May 2008 level).

bullets.title: TTD: Initiated at Sell by Rothschild ($11 PT); Walmart diversifying to Yahoo DSP
bullets.body: The Trade Desk fell 5.1% after Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated with a Sell rating and $11 price target. Separately, Walmart is reportedly diversifying programmatic ad spend away from Trade Desk to Yahoo's DSP, leveraging Yahoo's first-party data advantage. Both headlines represent structural headwinds for TTD's market position.

bullets.title: GEV/EPC bottleneck: Labor constraints the real gating item for data center and power buildout
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley Energy report flags EPC labor capacity (down from 9–11 to 4 viable contractors per NextEra) as the primary bottleneck for data center and power generation projects — not grid access. GE Vernova explicitly called EPC construction 'the gating item.' GEV had more Electrification orders in Q1 2026 than in the entire prior year. HUT, WULF, and IREN all emphasize execution certainty with tight EPC coordination as competitive advantages.

bullets.title: MU: Supply shortage extends to late 2027 per Micron EVP; SK Hynix gets additional NVDA HBM4 orders
bullets.body: Micron's EVP and Chief Business Officer said meaningful memory chip supply will only start coming online in late 2027, with ramps in 2028 — supporting pricing power through the cycle. NVIDIA has placed additional HBM4 orders with SK Hynix, reinforcing the supply tightness thesis.

bullets.title: AMZN: Data center networking breakthrough; adds Grok to Bedrock; $5B Anthropic Series H commitment
bullets.body: Amazon achieved a significant breakthrough in data center networking (Resilient Network Graphs architecture: 33% better throughput, 40% less power). Amazon is also in discussions to add SpaceX's Grok models to its Bedrock AI platform, and committed $5B of the $15B hyperscaler tranche in Anthropic's $65B Series H round at a $965B valuation.

bullets.title: TKO: +6.8% on FIFA World Cup hospitality record; TTD -5.1%; OMC initiated Neutral
bullets.body: TKO surged 6.8% after reporting FIFA World Cup hospitality package sales more than doubled the prior record with 500K+ deals purchased. In the same sector, Trade Desk fell 5.1% on Rothschild Sell initiation and Omnicom was initiated at Neutral with an $89 PT.
